stem: The U.S. divest-or-ban law for TikTok is best treated as which PESTEL bucket for forecasting firm strategy?

options.A: Legal constraint shaping permissible ownership structures
options.B: Economic signal changing real wages and consumer demand
options.C: Sociocultural shift changing tastes and identity norms
options.D: Technological shock changing platform architectures rapidly

stem: The EU opening DMA non-compliance investigations is, analytically, the clearest example of:

options.A: Legal force increasing compliance costs and design constraints
options.B: Economic force raising interest rates and credit spreads
options.C: Technological force reducing marginal costs via automation
options.D: Ecological force internalising emissions externalities quickly

stem: Apple/Meta being found in breach of DMA obligations most directly changes which firm-level risk surface?

options.A: Regulatory exposure that can compress platform take-rates
options.B: Buyer tastes that can shift demand across demographics
options.C: Supplier rivalry that can lower component input prices
options.D: Entry barriers that can increase incumbent differentiation

stem: RBI restrictions on Paytm Payments Bank most cleanly map to which PESTEL dimension?

options.A: Legal constraint tightening what transactions are allowed
options.B: Technological shock lowering the cost of digital identity
options.C: Sociocultural shift raising trust in mobile-first banking
options.D: Ecological shift pricing pollution into payment systems

stem: CrowdStrike’s 2024 outage is best framed as which PESTEL category when teaching “exogenous shock”?

options.A: Technological disruption cascading through interdependence
options.B: Political disruption from activism and lobbying coalitions
options.C: Legal disruption from new privacy rules and fines
options.D: Ecological disruption from climate volatility and floods

stem: The Red Sea shipping disruption is most defensibly placed where in PESTEL, if you must pick one primary driver?

options.A: Political risk altering trade routes and insurance terms
options.B: Technological shift increasing container vessel utilisation
options.C: Sociocultural shift changing consumption away from imports
options.D: Legal shift redefining antitrust standards for shipping

stem: In SCP logic, a move from fragmented to consolidated structure most reliably implies which conduct shift?

options.A: Greater price leadership and more tacit coordination risks
options.B: Lower switching costs and more buyer-led commoditisation
options.C: Faster entry and more micro-entrepreneurial turbulence
options.D: Lower exit barriers and more rapid capacity withdrawal

stem: Which statement captures the SCP causal direction as used in external analysis (not RBV)?

options.A: Structure shapes conduct, which shapes performance outcomes
options.B: Conduct shapes structure, which shapes performance outcomes
options.C: Performance shapes conduct, which shapes structure outcomes
options.D: Structure shapes resources, which shapes conduct outcomes

stem: “Velocity mapping” most directly fixes which PESTEL limitation?

options.A: Static listing that ignores speed and nonlinearity of change
options.B: Overemphasis on rivals rather than supplier bargaining power
options.C: Overuse of financial ratios rather than causal mechanisms
options.D: Confusion between strategic groups and industry boundaries

stem: A major antitrust remedies decision against Google (search) most naturally belongs to which analysis layer?

options.A: General environment constraint that reshapes industry rules
options.B: Internal capability audit that reshapes VRIO conclusions
options.C: Value chain analysis that reshapes activity configuration
options.D: Cultural analysis that reshapes mission and identity claims

stem: In PESTEL, NGO and social-movement pressure (e.g., reputational campaigns) is best treated as:

options.A: Political force affecting nonmarket strategy and legitimacy
options.B: Legal force automatically binding through statutory rules
options.C: Economic force moving interest rates and wage inflation
options.D: Technological force changing production process efficiency

stem: Which is the tightest distinction between Political and Legal in PESTEL?

options.A: Political is influence; legal is codified enforceable outcome
options.B: Political is culture; legal is consumer preference evolution
options.C: Political is technology; legal is platform infrastructure risk
options.D: Political is inflation; legal is monetary policy transmission

stem: “Blockbuster ignored streaming” is best read as which PESTEL interaction?

options.A: Technological shift plus sociocultural convenience preference
options.B: Legal shift plus ecological externality internalisation
options.C: Economic shift plus political activism against late fees
options.D: Ecological shift plus demographic aging and retirement

stem: Under SCP, why does a monopoly “produce less and charge more” in the canonical model?

options.A: Market power enables price-setting above marginal cost
options.B: Buyers collude, pushing prices below marginal cost
options.C: Suppliers diversify, forcing costs down via scale effects
options.D: Entrants discipline pricing through contestable markets

stem: If interest rates spike, which industry type is most structurally exposed in the “Economic” part of PESTEL?

options.A: Capital-intensive industries reliant on cheap financing
options.B: Labour-intensive industries with low fixed costs
options.C: Digitally-native industries with low marginal costs
options.D: Regulated utilities with stable rate-base returns

stem: A stricter data privacy regime most directly increases which cost category for a digital platform?

options.A: Compliance and redesign costs that raise fixed overheads
options.B: Variable production costs that scale linearly with users
options.C: Marketing costs that disappear through organic virality
options.D: Input costs that fall due to supplier fragmentation

stem: The best “PESTEL → strategy” move after a legal shock is typically:

options.A: Redesign choices and governance to regain legitimacy
options.B: Double down on price wars to deter all entrants
options.C: Ignore signals until performance metrics clearly fall
options.D: Substitute internal vision statements for external scanning

stem: Which is the cleanest industry boundary mistake in external analysis?

options.A: Treating “payments” and “banking” as identical industries
options.B: Identifying rivalry among direct substitutes as intense
options.C: Separating general environment from competitive forces
options.D: Noting that complements can raise willingness-to-pay

stem: When the initiating driver is geopolitical risk but the firm impact is inflation, the correct analytic discipline is:

options.A: Keep driver in Political, trace outcomes into Economic
options.B: Put everything in Economic since prices moved first
options.C: Put everything in Legal since routes changed by rules
options.D: Put everything in Technology due to logistics systems

stem: Which claim about PESTEL is most defensible?

options.A: It frames exogenous factors; it does not rank rivals
options.B: It predicts exact market share trajectories reliably
options.C: It replaces Five Forces as a profit model substitute
options.D: It is mainly an internal audit of firm resources

stem: In SCP, “Performance” is best operationalised as:

options.A: Profitability relative to cost of capital, not just profit
options.B: Revenue growth regardless of capital intensity and risk
options.C: Brand awareness regardless of pricing power and entry
options.D: Headcount growth regardless of productivity and margins

stem: Which best matches “nonmarket strategy” mentioned in Session 8?

options.A: Lobbying, litigation, coalition-building, and public framing
options.B: Capacity expansion, cost cutting, and product redesign
options.C: Vertical integration, scale economies, and procurement
options.D: Market segmentation, positioning, and pricing experiments

stem: A “technological” PESTEL factor is best defined as:

options.A: Applying knowledge to new products and processes
options.B: A new regulation imposing reporting and audits
options.C: A demographic change altering household structures
options.D: A macro shock changing unemployment and wages

stem: Why is “inflation is high” not enough as a PESTEL insight?

options.A: You must translate it into demand, costs, and pricing power
options.B: It already implies rivalry is low and entry barriers are high
options.C: It automatically means buyer power is weak and falling fast
options.D: It automatically means substitutes vanish due to scarcity

stem: The most accurate description of “exogenous shock” in this session is:

options.A: A factor outside firm control that can be monitored
options.B: A factor inside firm culture that can be engineered
options.C: A factor caused by rivals that can be fully prevented
options.D: A factor caused by buyers that can be contractually banned

stem: The EU’s DMA investigations most directly change which Five Forces element for a gatekeeper platform?

options.A: Threat of entry via mandated interoperability and access
options.B: Threat of substitutes via new consumer taste formation
options.C: Supplier power via higher chip input concentration
options.D: Rivalry via lower fixed costs in legacy manufacturing

stem: In Five Forces terms, Google’s default-distribution agreements primarily strengthen which barrier?

options.A: Switching and distribution barriers that deter new entrants
options.B: Scale barriers in steel production and bulk commodities
options.C: Labour barriers from unions and pension obligations
options.D: Product barriers from physical shelf-space scarcity

stem: A strong antitrust remedy that curtails default exclusivity most likely affects industry profit by:

options.A: Raising rivalry and entry pressure, compressing margins
options.B: Lowering buyer power, increasing take-rates sustainably
options.C: Lowering substitutes, stabilising premium pricing power
options.D: Raising exit barriers, preventing capacity discipline

stem: RBI constraints on a payments bank shift its Five Forces position primarily by:

options.A: Increasing regulatory constraints that limit strategic conduct
options.B: Decreasing supplier concentration for payment rails access
options.C: Decreasing rivalry by forcing all fintechs to consolidate
options.D: Increasing substitutes by lowering consumer search costs

stem: CrowdStrike outage: for many enterprises, the immediate Five Forces lesson is closest to:

options.A: Supplier power rises when switching is slow and risky
options.B: Buyer power rises when contracts are short and flexible
options.C: Entry threat rises when capital costs increase sharply
options.D: Rivalry falls when products commoditise fully

stem: Red Sea disruption most plausibly increases supplier power for shipping/insurance because:

options.A: Capacity tightens and routing risk raises switching frictions
options.B: Demand collapses and shipping rates become irrelevant
options.C: New entrants flood in with instant spare vessel capacity
options.D: Buyers integrate backward into shipbuilding immediately

stem: In Five Forces, complements matter because they:

options.A: Raise willingness-to-pay, altering industry demand curve
options.B: Always reduce rivalry by eliminating product differences
options.C: Always increase supplier power by concentrating inputs
options.D: Replace substitutes by legal decree and enforcement

stem: If a platform’s complement (e.g., app ecosystem) strengthens rapidly, the most precise profit implication is:

options.A: Value creation rises; value capture depends on bargaining power
options.B: Value capture rises automatically; power dynamics disappear
options.C: Rivalry disappears automatically; entry becomes impossible
options.D: Buyer power vanishes automatically; switching costs go to zero

stem: Which situation most clearly increases threat of substitutes rather than threat of entry?

options.A: A new workflow tool replaces meetings without being a rival firm
options.B: A new firm launches a copycat app with identical features
options.C: A supplier vertically integrates into end-user distribution
options.D: A buyer backward integrates into input manufacturing

stem: A key mistake in applying Five Forces to AI platforms is:

options.A: Treating complementors as rivals without mapping bargaining power
options.B: Measuring fixed costs while ignoring marginal cost entirely
options.C: Defining buyers as employees rather than paying customers
options.D: Ignoring internal resources while doing external analysis

stem: A market with high exit barriers tends to exhibit:

options.A: Sustained rivalry and price pressure even when demand falls
options.B: Rapid capacity withdrawal restoring profits instantly
options.C: High entry threat because sunk costs are low
options.D: Low buyer power because switching costs explode

stem: Strategic groups are not a “sixth force,” but they matter because they:

options.A: Localise rivalry where mobility barriers keep firms clustered
options.B: Replace substitutes by redefining the consumer utility function
options.C: Eliminate supplier power by pooling industry procurement
options.D: Remove regulation risk by aligning with political interests

stem: Reddit’s IPO is best used in this session to test which inference?

options.A: Public markets change governance pressure and risk tolerance
options.B: IPOs instantly raise entry barriers in social media markets
options.C: IPOs instantly remove substitutes through network effects
options.D: IPOs instantly collapse supplier power in adtech markets

stem: A “price war” in oligopoly is often irrational because:

options.A: Retaliation is likely, destroying joint industry profits
options.B: Buyers are fragmented, making retaliation impossible
options.C: Entry barriers are low, making war always optimal
options.D: Substitutes are absent, making price irrelevant

stem: Which factor is most likely to increase buyer power in B2B software?

options.A: Standardised features that make multi-vendor bids credible
options.B: Highly differentiated features that raise switching costs
options.C: Asset specificity that makes the buyer locked-in forever
options.D: Regulatory barriers that prevent buyer comparisons

stem: If a firm’s input is concentrated in one supplier and switching is costly, the most accurate label is:

options.A: High supplier power driven by differentiation and lock-in
options.B: High buyer power driven by fragmented demand and auctions
options.C: High rivalry driven by many similar small competitors
options.D: High entry threat driven by low capital requirements

stem: A legal mandate that requires “allowing alternative app stores” most plausibly affects:

options.A: Entry barriers and distribution access for potential rivals
options.B: Substitute threat by reducing consumer willingness-to-pay
options.C: Supplier power by concentrating semiconductor fabrication
options.D: Exit barriers by increasing stranded asset write-downs

stem: Which is the most Porterian way to talk about network effects?

options.A: As a structural source of switching costs and entry barriers
options.B: As an internal resource that guarantees sustained advantage
options.C: As a macroeconomic shock that increases unemployment
options.D: As a sociocultural trend that changes identity norms

stem: A firm launching its own chips to reduce dependence is best read as:

options.A: Vertical integration to blunt supplier bargaining power
options.B: Diversification to increase substitutes in the same industry
options.C: Retrenchment to increase exit barriers and rivalry
options.D: Collusion to reduce buyer bargaining power by fiat

stem: A high “threat of entry” does not require:

options.A: Low switching costs and low credible retaliation
options.B: Many substitutes that fulfil the same job-to-be-done
options.C: Access to distribution and low regulatory hurdles
options.D: Low scale economies and low capital requirements

stem: Which is the best “force-level” prediction when regulation raises compliance costs sharply?

options.A: Entry threat often falls if compliance is a fixed cost barrier
options.B: Entry threat always rises since regulators favour challengers
options.C: Buyer power always rises since buyers love compliance reports
options.D: Supplier power always falls since inputs become commoditised

stem: A strategy that improves “fit” across activities helps Five Forces by:

options.A: Making imitation costly and reducing price-based rivalry
options.B: Making substitutes illegal and removing buyer choice
options.C: Raising inflation and reducing wage growth pressures
options.D: Increasing supplier concentration and limiting procurement

stem: Which is the cleanest sign that rivalry is structurally high?

options.A: Slow growth plus high fixed costs plus undifferentiated offers
options.B: Fast growth plus strong differentiation plus low fixed costs
options.C: Strong complements plus rising demand plus low entry threat
options.D: High buyer switching costs plus high differentiation plus fit

stem: The best time to use Five Forces over PESTEL is when:

options.A: You need a profit-pool view from bargaining and rivalry
options.B: You need macro scanning of exogenous shocks and trends
options.C: You need internal capability assessment and VRIO logic
options.D: You need leadership psychology and upper echelons theory

stem: The sharpest conceptual difference between entry barriers and mobility barriers is:

options.A: Entry blocks new firms; mobility blocks repositioning across groups
options.B: Entry blocks substitutes; mobility blocks complements from forming
options.C: Entry blocks buyers; mobility blocks suppliers from consolidating
options.D: Entry blocks inflation; mobility blocks interest-rate transmission

stem: A strategic group map’s primary purpose is to:

options.A: Explain intra-industry heterogeneity in rivalry and returns
options.B: Replace Five Forces by adding a sixth universal force
options.C: Predict macro shocks better than PESTEL scanning
options.D: Prove internal resources are always sufficient for success

stem: The clearest empirical sign of a mobility barrier is:

options.A: Persistent performance gaps across groups despite imitation
options.B: Rapid movement of firms across groups with low cost
options.C: Instant convergence of prices and service levels across firms
options.D: Identical cost structures across all firms in the industry

stem: In airlines, a hub-and-spoke network is best treated as:

options.A: A mobility barrier protecting a strategic group position
options.B: A substitute increasing rivalry by lowering switching costs
options.C: A macroeconomic factor in the Economic PESTEL category
options.D: A legal factor created by court rulings and mandates

stem: If a low-cost airline adds lounges and business-class seats, the deepest risk is:

options.A: Cost creep that erodes the low-cost strategic logic
options.B: Entry threat rising because capital requirements fall
options.C: Supplier power rising because fuel becomes scarce
options.D: Substitute threat rising because trains become faster

stem: Strategic groups are most useful when industries have:

options.A: Multiple viable configurations of scope, price, and service
options.B: Perfect competition with identical firms and no differences
options.C: Monopolies with no rivals and no intra-industry variation
options.D: Pure monopolistic competition with zero scale effects

stem: A platform moving from “creator tools” to “payments bank” is blocked by which barrier class most often?

options.A: Regulatory licensing and compliance as mobility barriers
options.B: Threat of substitutes from competing creator platforms
options.C: Rivalry intensity from many small local restaurants
options.D: Supplier power from shipbuilders and port operators

stem: Paytm’s regulatory constraints illustrate a mobility barrier because they:

options.A: Prevent straightforward expansion of scope within finance
options.B: Remove rivalry by forcing all fintechs to coordinate
options.C: Eliminate buyer power by creating universal switching costs
options.D: Collapse substitutes by creating stronger network effects

stem: In strategic group logic, the fiercest rivalry is typically:

options.A: Within the same group where offerings and economics overlap
options.B: Across distant groups where offerings are structurally distinct
options.C: Only between complements that jointly raise demand
options.D: Only between suppliers who sell inputs to all firms

stem: A firm’s attempt to “move upmarket” fails most often because:

options.A: Activity systems and brand signals are slow to rebuild
options.B: Buyer power disappears and customers stop comparing prices
options.C: Substitutes vanish and consumers lose alternative options
options.D: Entry threat collapses and capital markets become irrelevant

stem: The most precise relationship between mobility barriers and entry barriers is:

options.A: Mobility can be high even when entry is moderate
options.B: Mobility and entry always move in the same direction
options.C: Mobility matters only when entry threat is zero
options.D: Mobility disappears when substitutes increase rapidly

stem: A strategic group map is least useful when:

options.A: Firms are nearly identical and compete only on price
options.B: Firms differ widely in scope, service, and cost structure
options.C: Product differentiation creates stable clusters of rivals
options.D: Mobility barriers block rapid repositioning attempts

stem: For social platforms, “algorithmic distribution” often acts like:

options.A: A mobility barrier because it is path-dependent and cumulative
options.B: A substitute because it replaces user attention entirely
options.C: A supplier because it is purchased as an external input
options.D: An ecological factor because it changes carbon intensity

stem: TikTok’s forced restructuring is likely to alter which group boundary most?

options.A: “National-security compliant” vs “cross-border controlled” platforms
options.B: “Premium priced” vs “low priced” consumer goods sellers
options.C: “High capex” vs “low capex” heavy manufacturing firms
options.D: “Old economy” vs “new economy” firms in general

stem: In group terms, “mobility barriers” are closest to:

options.A: Structural walls that make imitation costly and slow
options.B: Marketing slogans that can be changed in a week
options.C: Buyer preferences that shift randomly without drivers
options.D: One-time shocks that disappear without lasting effects

stem: The key error students make with group maps is:

options.A: Using too many dimensions and losing interpretability
options.B: Using too few dimensions and making it too simple
options.C: Treating groups as moral categories of “good” and “bad”
options.D: Treating groups as identical to PESTEL categories

stem: “Premium trust” in airlines is best treated as what kind of asset in mobility terms?

options.A: Reputation capital that is slow to build and easy to lose
options.B: A commodity input that can be purchased instantly
options.C: A substitute that replaces safety engineering entirely
options.D: A political mandate that automatically ensures demand

stem: Which is the best example of “mobility barrier via regulation”?

options.A: A licence requirement that restricts product scope expansion
options.B: A new entrant copying a UI and buying ads cheaply
options.C: A substitute product solving the job differently
options.D: A buyer negotiating discounts via bulk purchases

stem: Strategic groups connect to Five Forces because:

options.A: Forces differ in intensity by group location and economics
options.B: Forces become identical once the industry boundary is set
options.C: Forces disappear when groups are mapped correctly
options.D: Forces are purely internal capabilities, not external structure

stem: A “low-cost” group is protected most by:

options.A: Cost system discipline and activity fit, not single features
options.B: A single ad campaign that changes brand perception quickly
options.C: A one-off discount that permanently locks-in customers
options.D: A legal decree that prevents consumers from switching

stem: If a firm tries to span two distant groups, the biggest structural danger is:

options.A: Internal contradictions that destroy both cost and differentiation
options.B: Lower entry barriers that suddenly invite thousands of entrants
options.C: Lower substitutes that make demand perfectly inelastic
options.D: Lower supplier power that makes inputs cheaper over time

stem: A “strategic group” is best defined as:

options.A: Firms with similar strategies competing on similar dimensions
options.B: Firms with identical missions and identical internal cultures
options.C: Firms facing identical macro shocks in the general environment
options.D: Firms that share the same suppliers and the same buyers

stem: A group boundary becomes a “barrier” when:

options.A: Moving across it requires large, irreversible commitments
options.B: Moving across it requires only messaging and rebranding
options.C: Moving across it requires only a short-term discount
options.D: Moving across it requires only hiring a new CEO

stem: The sharpest reason strategic groups matter for students is:

options.A: They prevent naïve “one-industry one-strategy” thinking
options.B: They eliminate the need for industry structure analysis
options.C: They remove the need for market definition discipline
options.D: They substitute for quantitative performance measures

stem: A common “category error” is to treat DMA as mainly technological because it affects app design. Why is that wrong?

options.A: The initiating driver is legal constraint, not innovation
options.B: The driver is inflation transmission, not rules or mandates
options.C: The driver is demographic change, not institutional policy
options.D: The driver is ecological scarcity, not platform governance

stem: If a shock increases fixed compliance costs, the most Porteresque prediction is:

options.A: Entry threat falls when fixed costs deter small challengers
options.B: Entry threat rises because compliance is a demand stimulator
options.C: Supplier power collapses because suppliers hate paperwork
options.D: Rivalry disappears because firms become more ethical

stem: A strategy memo that lists “inflation, AI, ESG, geopolitics” but offers no mechanisms is failing at:

options.A: Translating environment into causal impacts on profitability
options.B: Calculating WACC precisely for each business segment
options.C: Writing a mission statement with emotionally resonant verbs
options.D: Choosing a new organisational structure for ambidexterity

stem: A firm facing Red Sea shipping disruption should not conclude automatically that:

options.A: Higher freight rates imply higher pricing power for the firm
options.B: Higher freight rates can raise costs and shift demand
options.C: Rerouting can increase lead times and working capital
options.D: Risk can raise insurance costs and supplier leverage

stem: TikTok’s restructuring risk is analytically closest to which Five Forces channel?

options.A: Regulatory constraint reshaping entry, conduct, and capture
options.B: Supplier concentration reshaping semiconductor input prices
options.C: Substitute pressure reshaping demand away from short video
options.D: Rivalry decline reshaping the number of active platforms

stem: A subtle but crucial distinction: “buyers are powerful” means they can:

options.A: Force price concessions by credible switching or volume
options.B: Force suppliers to merge and reduce input variety
options.C: Force substitutes to disappear from adjacent industries
options.D: Force entry barriers to rise through scale economies

stem: The cleanest indicator that an industry is in “shakeout/maturity” is:

options.A: Growth slows and consolidation rises as weaker firms exit
options.B: Growth explodes and new entrants flood in monthly
options.C: Product meaning shifts and consumers adopt new norms
options.D: Regulation disappears and compliance costs fall sharply

stem: Google’s monopoly remedies debate is best used to teach:

options.A: How rule changes can rewire entry barriers and distribution
options.B: How culture change alone can eliminate competitive forces
options.C: How inflation reduces substitutes by lowering innovation
options.D: How demographics automatically raise switching costs

stem: In external analysis, “industry attractiveness” is primarily about:

options.A: Structural profit potential, not a firm’s current share
options.B: A firm’s internal capabilities and VRIO resources
options.C: The CEO’s charisma and leadership narrative skill
options.D: The firm’s mission statement and ethical commitments

stem: A correct reading of “value capture is a power game” is:

options.A: Bargaining power decides who keeps surplus, not who creates it
options.B: Innovation always captures value regardless of structure
options.C: Complements always capture value regardless of contracts
options.D: Buyers never capture value because they do not produce

stem: A “strategic group” analysis adds most when Five Forces says:

options.A: “Moderate” overall, but profit differences persist across clusters
options.B: “Low rivalry” overall, and all firms earn identical returns
options.C: “High entry” overall, and no firm survives past a year
options.D: “High substitutes” overall, and demand is already collapsing

stem: The best one-line definition of “mobility barrier” is:

options.A: Costly constraint preventing repositioning across strategic clusters
options.B: Costly constraint preventing any new entrant from entering
options.C: Costly constraint preventing substitutes from being invented
options.D: Costly constraint preventing buyers from negotiating price

stem: A firm that copies a market leader under uncertainty is showing:

options.A: Mimetic isomorphism as a legitimacy-seeking response
options.B: Predatory pricing as a deliberate rivalry escalator
options.C: Perfect competition as a structural inevitability
options.D: Complementarity as a demand-expansion mechanism

stem: Reddit’s IPO is most useful here to ask: “What changed structurally?” The most defensible answer is:

options.A: Governance and disclosure pressures changed, not the industry map
options.B: Entry barriers collapsed because IPOs create public liquidity
options.C: Supplier power vanished because the ticker symbol is new
options.D: Substitutes declined because users prefer listed companies

stem: A firm hit by Paytm-like regulatory constraints should first test:

options.A: Whether its “industry definition” must narrow to allowed scope
options.B: Whether substitutes vanished because regulation became strict
options.C: Whether suppliers became fragmented because audits increased
options.D: Whether rivalry fell because compliance teams are expensive

stem: In PESTEL, the most precise reason “unemployment is low” matters is:

options.A: Wage pressure rises, shifting costs and bargaining dynamics
options.B: Entry barriers rise because firms cannot hire CEOs
options.C: Substitutes vanish because labour becomes scarce
options.D: Rivalry disappears because demand becomes predictable

stem: Which statement is most accurate about “externalities” in ecological analysis?

options.A: Costs not priced in can later return as regulation or backlash
options.B: Costs not priced in always vanish because markets are efficient
options.C: Costs not priced in always reduce rivalry across all industries
options.D: Costs not priced in always increase complements immediately

stem: A firm claims “we will beat rivals by working harder.” The best Session 8 critique is:

options.A: Structure and power can dominate effort; analyse constraints first
options.B: Effort guarantees monopoly power if culture is strong
options.C: Effort eliminates substitutes because customers admire hustle
options.D: Effort lowers interest rates by improving investor sentiment

stem: The most rigorous use of “strategic groups” in a case write-up is to:

options.A: Specify axes, justify clusters, and name mobility barriers
options.B: List every competitor alphabetically with market shares
options.C: Replace Five Forces with a colourful diagram and quotes
options.D: Provide mission statements and values of each firm

stem: A robust five-forces memo should avoid:

options.A: Treating “competition” as rivalry only, ignoring other forces
options.B: Defining buyers as buyers, not confusing them with users
options.C: Describing substitutes as different solutions to the same need
options.D: Stating which force is strongest and why, with evidence

stem: When students confuse complements and substitutes, the telltale sign is they:

options.A: Treat “charging stations” as replacing EVs rather than enabling
options.B: Treat “new entrants” as solving the same job differently
options.C: Treat “buyers” as always being the end consumer
options.D: Treat “rivalry” as always being low when growth is high

stem: A correct interpretation of “price taker” is:

options.A: Firm faces elastic demand at market price and lacks power
options.B: Firm can set price above marginal cost without losing volume
options.C: Firm can collude costlessly because rivals are fragmented
options.D: Firm can block entry because switching costs are infinite

stem: If you must write one sentence that unifies Session 8, the best is:

options.A: Define where you compete before deciding how you compete
options.B: Decide how you compete before defining where you compete
options.C: Ignore structure because leadership can override all forces
options.D: Ignore environment because purpose guarantees profitability
